text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Sweden must be a member of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) in order to join the euro, but Sweden disagrees.
- The stockmarket cheered the appointment of Fred Hassan as the managing director of Swedish-U.S drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn .
- European Union Finance Ministers say Sweden must lower taxes and cut public spending even more in order to join Europe's economic and monetary union.

- Not all high-tech companies are moving production out of Sweden. Pacemaker producer Pacesetter recently closed production in Miami and expanded in Jarfalla, Sweden, where it employeed 100 new staff.
- Some 40 percent of Swedish-trained civil engineers say they would be interested in working overseas at some time. Some 80 percent say they would be willing to work abroad at least three years.

- Swedish clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz is prepared to move the company headquarters overseas. "It's the task of politicians to see that attractive possibilities for investors and entrepreneurs are established," managing director Stefan Persson says.

- Only 32 percent of Swedes in a poll believe the phasing out of nuclear power is the right decision. Some 53 percent believe the decision by the Swedish government to start shutting down the country's nuclear power plants is wrong.

- Pharmacia & Upjohn's new managing director Fred Hassan told a telephone conference that he would establish a common corporate culture in the Swedish-U.S. firm, bring new products to the market and formulate a strategic plan for long-term growth. The share gained 15.5 crowns or 6.4 percent after Hassan's comments.
